label: One governing standard can supply beneficiary credit
summary: An existential omission witness suffices when coverage has supplied an operative plan and recognition applies to every required benefit in an operative plan. The mixed assignment preserves the instrumental plan as genuinely operative while a second operative plan requires the distinct recipient's esse credit. Thus existential rejection can hold with universal rejection false. With only the instrumental plan operative, even existential rejection fails while recipient willing, end direction and actuality-goodness coextension can hold. The assertions compare a fixed selected-world assignment. See Which operative standard needs to count the recipient's esse? in docs/notes/divine-love-goodness-bridge.md.
blocker: Identify a criterion for the same giver's production of this recipient, independent of the resulting output, and evidence that an operative standard requires esse credit to this recipient as its own good.
